clue.text: Honouring BBC boss receives terrible reaction

indicators.note: the boss's letters take in the scrambled word, holding it between them

parts.note: the head of the BBC is its Director-General, abbreviated DG

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters of the word after it are jumbled

explanation.surface: The head of the BBC gets a dreadful response to some decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' scrambles the reaction word to ECORATIN; 'receives' sets it between the two letters of the boss's title, Director-General.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorating someone means awarding them a medal or honour, so it is honouring them.

clue.text: Physician vacated internship — wimp!

parts.note: Dr is the title of a doctor or physician

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word stay

explanation.surface: A doctor walks out of an internship and is called a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacated' empties INTERNSHIP to its ends, IP.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is informal British slang for a feeble, spineless person, a weakling.

clue.text: Sailors love leaving newcomer on the rocks

indicators.note: leaving signals that the love letter departs from the newcomer word
on the rocks means wrecked, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Sailors abandon a new arrival when the ship is wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O out of NEWCOMER and rearrange the remaining NEWCMER.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewmen are the members of a ship's crew, so they are sailors.

clue.text: Being born again, Republican fashioned a nicer country

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made, so the letters are formed anew

parts.note: a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A born-again Republican creates a kinder nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' rearranges A NICER into EINCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Reincarnation is the rebirth of a soul in a new body after death.

clue.text: Understand journalist's after traitor being held up and shot at

indicators.note: after places the understand and journalist pieces following the traitor piece
held up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, a reversal

parts.note: a rat is someone who betrays others
to get something is to understand it
ED, an editor, is the stock crossword journalist; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A journalist grasps that a traitor held at gunpoint was fired upon.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'being held up' means read upwards; 'after' says the understanding and journalist pieces come behind the traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Being targeted means being aimed at, as a shot is aimed at its mark.

clue.text: I grumble over girl

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: to moan is to complain or grumble

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns I MOAN round.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a girl's name, the biblical mother-in-law of Ruth.

clue.text: Desire sorceress, not wife

indicators.note: the word 'not' tells us the wife's letter is left out of the sorceress

parts.note: a sorceress is a female practitioner of magic, a witch
W is the standard abbreviation for wife in genealogy and crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a sorceress who is not married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the W from WITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving or longing for something, a synonym of a desire.

clue.text: Find fault in character's weight

indicators.note: in places the fault-finding word inside the character word

parts.note: tone is character or quality, as in the tone of a place; 's is 'is'
to nag is to keep criticising, finding fault

explanation.surface: Someone criticises a person's heft.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage is a measure of weight or cargo capacity, especially of ships.

clue.text: Good Lord tells the drunk to support that chap

indicators.note: in a down clue the jumbled letters sit below the chap and so hold him up

parts.note: he refers to a male person, that chap

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A clergyman tells a drunk to look after another man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges TELLS THE into LLSTEETH, under HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell's teeth is an old exclamation of surprise or annoyance, like Good Lord.

clue.text: Ancient tribe a danger for motorists going to North Island

parts.note: ice on the road is a hazard for drivers
N is the compass abbreviation for north
I is the usual abbreviation for island on maps

explanation.surface: Drivers heading for New Zealand's North Island face a hazard, oddly linked with an ancient people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' simply joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were a Celtic people of eastern Britain led by Boudicca against the Romans.

clue.text: Mouth passage from violent cartoon by a liberal

indicators.note: violent suggests the word is roughly thrown about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal in British politics

explanation.surface: A rough cartoon and a liberal commentator somehow lead to an oral channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' scrambles the cartoon to give ROOTCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A root canal is the channel inside a tooth's root, so a passage within the mouth.

clue.text: Vet office involved with sect saving money

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A veterinary office linked with a cult is said to be thrifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges VET OFFICE and SECT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Cost-effective means giving good value for what is spent, so economical or thrifty.

clue.text: Clash with minister that's manipulated restaurant awards

indicators.note: manipulated means handled and reworked, so the letters of both words are rearranged together

explanation.surface: A clash with a government minister has been stage-managed by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manipulated' rearranges the letters of CLASH and MINISTER together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Michelin Guide grants stars, from one to three, to fine-dining establishments as marks of quality.

clue.text: Alleged snobs mixed with elite

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Supposed snobs are mingling with the upper crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges SNOBS and ELITE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means apparent or professed, as something alleged or claimed may not be true.

clue.text: Senator briefly judges guards

parts.note: Sen. is the short form of Senator
to try a case is to judge it in court, so judges are tries

explanation.surface: A senator in short order passes judgement on the guards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentries are soldiers posted to keep watch, standing guard over a place.

clue.text: Vicar standing by before worship

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title
ere is an old word meaning before

explanation.surface: A vicar waits on hand ahead of the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing by' just places the two pieces next to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere is to hold in deep respect or veneration, a verb close to worship.

clue.text: Perhaps swimming off Isle of Wight is disrespectful

parts.note: a swimmer is in the water, so in is an example
the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England

explanation.surface: Swimming off the Isle of Wight might be seen as rude.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the stretch of sea between the Isle of Wight, an island off southern England, and the mainland.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent means rude and lacking respect, a synonym of disrespectful.

clue.text: Catch nurse on break coming back

parts.note: EN stands for enrolled nurse

indicators.note: coming back tells us the break word is read from right to left

parts.note: to part is to break or split apart

explanation.surface: A nurse returns to the ward after a break and gets caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns only the break word round, giving TRAP; 'on' just sets the nurse beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to snare or trick them, the same as to catch them.

clue.text: Adolescent upset agent employing two Europeans

indicators.note: employing means taking on, so the jumbled letters hold the pair inside
upset means knocked over, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European; two give EE

explanation.surface: A troubled agent hires a couple of continental staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' jumbles the agent to TNAGE, and 'employing' has those letters take the two Europeans in.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenage describes someone between thirteen and nineteen, in adolescence.

clue.text: Extinguish prisoner's cigarette when restraining posh females

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so the cigarette word encloses the other letters

parts.note: snout is prison slang for tobacco or a cigarette
U means upper-class, posh, in British usage
F is short for female; FF gives the plural

explanation.surface: A prisoner's smoke is put out while upper-class women are held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restraining' is the container signal. U for posh comes from the old British U and non-U labels for upper-class and other speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To snuff out a flame or candle is to put it out, a phrase for extinguish.

clue.text: Cover old bulb at either end with sulphur and salt

parts.note: the word bulb has the same letter at its start and finish
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
to cure meat is to preserve it with salt

explanation.surface: Instructions for covering an old bulb with chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: BULB both begins and ends with B, so one B is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to hide or cover it from view.

clue.text: Cop with rifle cases manoeuvring secretive fighters

indicators.note: manoeuvring means shifting into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A policeman shifting gun cases about looks like covert soldiers at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' rearranges COP, RIFLE and CASES together.
explanation.definitionFit: Special forces are elite military units that carry out covert operations, hence fighters who work in secret.

clue.text: One enters into new role as banker

indicators.note: enters into means goes inside, so the numeral is placed within the scrambled letters
new indicates the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a fresh role as a bank employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns ROLE into LORE; 'enters into' puts I inside. A banker in crosswords is often a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is France's longest river, and a river is something with banks.

clue.text: Message former partner during race meeting

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the partner sits inside the race letters

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Someone messages an old flame while at the races.
explanation.definitionFit: A text is a short message sent by phone.

clue.text: Tolerate spoiled anise sauce

parts.note: to bear something is to put up with it

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined or messed up, so the letters of the spice word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with a sauce ruined by aniseed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' jumbles the spice word into NAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Béarnaise is a classic French sauce of butter, egg yolk, shallots and tarragon.

clue.text: Occupied? That is, occupied by students

indicators.note: the abbreviation is filled by the students' letters, which sit inside it

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, meaning that is
NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a room is taken and is told students have it.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word is the trick: the first 'occupied' is the definition, the second, with 'by', is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in use, like a toilet or a phone line, is engaged or occupied.

clue.text: Like two (but not three) in a plane

definitions.meaning: two is divisible by two while three is not, so it describes a number of that kind
lying in a single plane means flat and level

explanation.surface: A puzzle about two passengers on an aircraft, not three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft; here it is a flat surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Even describes numbers divisible by two, and also surfaces that are flat and level.

clue.text: Money paid for somewhere to live?

definitions.meaning: a sum handed over to resolve a dispute or claim
a place where people have settled, such as a village or colony

explanation.surface: A question about paying money for a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement is both a payment agreed to end a claim and a community where people have made homes.
